first_impression.reaction: My assistant flagged it because we are deciding how large the bridal party should be, with cousins flying in from Sydney and London. The first line is calm and not selling: "Because a wedding is easier, and happier, with people you trust beside you." She summarised the history. I read Queen Victoria, the numbers section, the destination section and the close myself.

journey.quote: This guide follows the bridesmaid from the wedding feasts of classical Athens to Queen Victoria's twelve in white, then turns to the decisions in front of you now: maid or matron of honour, how many to ask, bridesmen, and asking friends to travel.
journey.reaction: Clear. It tells my assistant where the useful part is, without fuss.

journey.section: 1. Why do we have bridesmaids today?
journey.quote: The [Oxford Dictionary of Proverbs](https://www.oxfordreference.com/display/10.1093/acref/9780198734901.001.0001/acref-9780198734901-e-248) traces the saying.
journey.reaction: A reference book link after a line about mouthwash adverts. It reads like a school essay. My assistant skipped it.

journey.quote: The [Oxford Classical Dictionary](https://www.oxfordreference.com/display/10.1093/acref/9780199545568.001.0001/acref-9780199545568-e-3980) sets out the ceremony.
journey.reaction: Sending me elsewhere again. An authority would simply tell me.

journey.section: 3. Queen Victoria's bridesmaids and royal attendants
journey.quote: She had twelve bridesmaids, all the eldest daughters of peers.
journey.reaction: This is the part that speaks to families like mine. A large party chosen by standing, not just friendship. I read on.

journey.section: 3. Queen Victoria's bridesmaids and royal attendants
journey.quote: A long train or cathedral veil needs one or two named attendants, briefed and rehearsed on the actual aisle, steps and turns of your ceremony venue.
journey.reaction: Good. Someone has watched a train go wrong on a staircase. This is how a planner thinks, not a writer.

journey.section: 3. Queen Victoria's bridesmaids and royal attendants
journey.quote: Prince Albert designed a gift for the twelve: an eagle-shaped turquoise brooch, taken from the heraldic German eagle.
journey.reaction: A commissioned, meaningful gift. That is the level I think at.

journey.section: 6. How many bridesmaids should you have?
journey.quote: **What does the space allow?** A small chapel or a clifftop ceremony may suit three, not ten.
journey.reaction: Sensible, but every example here is small. Nothing for a party of twelve walking in front of 300 guests.

journey.section: 7. What bridesmaids and the maid of honour do, before and on the day
journey.quote: For a playful take, see [a peek inside a celebrity bridesmaid kit](/trending/whats-inside-rei-germars-bridesmaid-kit).
journey.reaction: A celebrity gossip link next to Queen Victoria. It cheapens the page.

journey.section: 7. What bridesmaids and the maid of honour do, before and on the day
journey.quote: **The details.** Tissues, pins, a phone charger, and a quiet word with the photographer.
journey.reaction: Fine for a friend's role, but with a large party my concern is the opposite: who stops attendants posting the morning on social media.

journey.quote: Who covers flights and accommodation, and is that the same for every attendant?
journey.reaction: In my family this is not a question. Our side covers it. The whole section assumes a shared-cost conversation, which is written for a different client.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller advises getting travel insurance whoever you are and wherever you are going, and treats the right policy as essential as a passport.
journey.reaction: Government consumer advice. My attendants' travel is handled by the family office. I want to hear how the planner manages arrivals, not reminders to buy insurance.

journey.quote: Sharing the itinerary with family at home and carrying hard copies of flight, accommodation and event bookings are sensible habits for the whole party.
journey.reaction: Backpacker tips. This is where my assistant would stop forwarding.

journey.quote: **One contact.** Name one person the venue team can reach about the party's timings.
journey.reaction: Correct. One channel, not twelve phones ringing the venue.

journey.quote: One advisor is your single point of contact, works in your time zone and confirms inclusions in writing.
journey.reaction: Dubai time matters to me, so that is welcome. Still nothing about scale, exclusive use or security.

journey.quote: For the traditions, places and people that shape a wedding, [read the free digital magazine](/magazine?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=why-do-we-have-bridesmaids&utm_content=primary).
The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and your advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Quiet and professional. No 'from' price, no discount talk. 'Inclusions' leans towards package language, but acceptable.

unanswered_questions: Have they delivered weddings of 200 to 400 guests with a large bridal party and exclusive use of the property?
How do they protect privacy with attendants and guests: phone and social media rules, vendor NDAs?
Can they arrange private transfers and accommodation for attendants arriving from several countries, billed to the family office?
Can they work with our own security team alongside the venue's?
Can they source or commission bespoke attendant gifts and outfits, and coordinate fittings across Dubai, Sydney and London?
Is there a private or referral channel to someone senior?

turn_offs_found.why: Repeated citations in the body (Oxford Reference twice, the Royal Collection Trust, the V&A, Cambridge Dictionary twice, Smartraveller) make the brand sound like it is borrowing authority rather than having it.
Pitches the destination section at a standard traveller and points me to a government website instead of showing what the planner handles.

turn_offs_found.quote: Who pays for outfits and hair, and does anyone need a different arrangement?
turn_offs_found.why: Cost-splitting questions frame the wedding around budgets, which tells me I am being treated like a standard client.

would_share_with: My assistant, to add attendant privacy and travel logistics questions to the planner shortlist
My sister, who will lead the party, for the section on the train and the lead attendant's role

cta_reaction.why: Understated, fee agreed in writing, my time zone, no price. But I don't fill in web forms, and nothing on the page shows they have handled my scale, privacy or security. Through my assistant or a referral, possibly.

top_3_changes: Remove visible sourcing in body copy (both Oxford Reference links, the Royal Collection Trust, V&A and Cambridge Dictionary lines, the Smartraveller line) so the voice states facts with authority.

Rebalance the destination section away from consumer travel tips (insurance, hard copies, who pays) towards how a planner looks after a travelling bridal party: arrivals, transfers, accommodation and one channel to the venue, if true.
Add one understated line acknowledging larger parties and privacy (attendants and social media on the morning), and drop the celebrity kit link and 'free' from the magazine line.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes the exact sentence from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, assistant reads first, cares about scale, privacy and discretion)
No invented brand facts; capability gaps listed as unanswered questions
Ignored HTML comments, image slots, CTA placeholders and VERIFY markers
Title and deferred business details not treated as must-fix; no price requested; no 'how we know' lines requested, per orchestrator
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection; every turn-off has a why

open_questions.question: The orchestrator said the brand voice never discusses sourcing, yet the draft names and links Oxford Reference (twice), the Royal Collection Trust, the V&A, Cambridge Dictionary (twice) and Smartraveller in body copy. Reported as over-explaining; please check against the brand voice guide.

assumptions: Layla is reading because she is deciding on a large bridal party with relatives travelling; the persona card doesn't say so.
Her assistant read the page first and summarised, per decision_behaviour.
